questions.q: A color photo loaded as a NumPy array has shape (512, 512, 3). What does that mean?
options: 512 rows, 512 columns and 3 color channels per pixel
questions.explain: Images are 3-D arrays of integers (height, width, channels).

questions.q: OpenCV loads color images as BGR while most other libraries assume RGB. What's the classic symptom if you forget?
options: Colors look wrong: reds and blues swapped
questions.explain: Convert with cv2.cvtColor when passing images between libraries.

questions.q: What is the usual dtype and value range of an 8-bit image?
questions.explain: Arithmetic on uint8 can overflow or wrap, so convert before math.

questions.q: Why is HSV useful for color-based segmentation?
options: It separates hue from brightness, so a color can be selected more robustly under lighting changes
questions.explain: Hue/saturation/value are easier to threshold than RGB.

questions.q: Which interpolation is the usual choice for shrinking an image?
questions.explain: Area averaging reduces aliasing when downscaling.

questions.q: You resize 1000x500 to 200x200. What goes wrong?
options: The aspect ratio is distorted; compute the other dimension from the ratio

questions.q: Why measure interpolation quality with MSE against the original?
options: It gives a number for how much detail was lost after downscale-then-upscale
questions.explain: Lower error means closer to the original.

questions.q: Does an RGB to HSV and back round trip return the original?
options: Essentially yes, within small rounding differences
questions.explain: Rounding to integers causes tiny differences.

questions.q: What does convolving an image with a 3x3 box kernel do?
options: Averages each pixel with its neighbours, blurring the image
questions.explain: The kernel slides across the image computing weighted sums.

questions.q: Why did the hand-written convolution disagree with cv2.filter2D at first?
options: Border handling and correlation versus convolution details differ; padding mode must match
questions.explain: The lesson investigated and resolved it.

questions.q: Which kernel type responds strongly at edges?
options: A gradient kernel such as Sobel
questions.explain: Edges are places where intensity changes quickly.

questions.q: What does sharpening do conceptually?
options: Boosts high-frequency detail by subtracting a blurred version or using a center-weighted kernel

questions.q: What advantage does Otsu's method have over a fixed threshold of 127?
options: It computes a threshold from the image's own histogram instead of guessing

questions.q: When is adaptive thresholding better than a global threshold?
options: When lighting varies across the image
questions.explain: It computes a threshold per neighbourhood.

questions.q: What does morphological opening do?
options: Erosion followed by dilation, removing small isolated noise

questions.q: What's morphological closing for?
options: Filling small gaps and holes inside foreground objects

questions.q: Why did area filtering alone not give the right coin count?
options: Non-coin blobs of similar area passed, so a shape measure like circularity was needed

questions.q: What does cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL return?
What does circularity (4*pi*area/perimeter^2) equal for a perfect circle?
questions.explain: Lower values mean less round shapes.

questions.q: What does the raw contour count include besides real objects?
options: Noise blobs and fragments, which is why filtering matters
questions.explain: The lesson started at 33 raw contours.

questions.q: What is a good keypoint?
options: A distinctive location (corner or blob) that can be found again in another view
questions.explain: Descriptors then describe it for matching.

questions.q: What does ORB provide that Harris corners alone don't?
options: Keypoints plus binary descriptors for matching

questions.q: The lesson measured ORB under 45-degree rotation and 2x scale. Why measure instead of assume?
options: Textbook invariance claims can be weaker in practice, especially for large scale changes

questions.q: What distinguishes SIFT from ORB?
options: SIFT uses floating-point descriptors and is heavier; ORB is fast with binary descriptors

questions.q: What does RANSAC do in findHomography?
options: Fits the transform to inlier matches while ignoring outlier (wrong) matches
questions.explain: Random sampling finds a consensus model.

questions.q: What does a homography represent?
options: A 3x3 projective transform mapping points between two views of a plane
questions.explain: Used for stitching and document alignment.

questions.q: Why compare the recovered homography to a known ground truth?
options: To measure how accurately the algorithm recovers a transform it was never told

questions.q: What happens if many matches are wrong and you skip RANSAC?
options: The estimated transform can be badly distorted by outliers

questions.q: Why use augmentation when training?
options: To expose the model to plausible variations and improve generalization
questions.explain: Flips, crops and jitter simulate real variation.

questions.q: What does SSIM measure?
options: Structural similarity between two images (1 is identical)

questions.q: What does cutout do?
options: Masks a random patch so the model can't rely on one region

questions.q: When is a horizontal flip a bad augmentation?
options: When orientation carries meaning, such as digits or text
questions.explain: Choose augmentations that preserve the label.

questions.q: What did the lesson find about Haar cascades in OpenCV 5.0?
options: This install no longer exposes CascadeClassifier

questions.q: Where does template matching break?
options: With scale and rotation changes of the target
questions.explain: It compares raw pixels at a fixed scale and orientation.

questions.q: What does cv2.matchTemplate return?
options: A similarity map whose peak marks the best location
questions.explain: Use minMaxLoc to find the peak.

questions.q: Why is template matching dangerous when pushed beyond its limits?
options: It can return a confident-looking location that is wrong

questions.q: What are the document scanner's main steps?
options: Edges, find the page contour, order its four corners, perspective-warp, then threshold

questions.q: Why order the four corners consistently?
options: The perspective transform needs matched source and destination corner order

questions.q: The project used a synthetic scene. What does the lesson say about that?
options: It states plainly that the input is synthetic while the pipeline is real

questions.q: What does getPerspectiveTransform produce?
options: A 3x3 matrix mapping four source points to four destination points

questions.q: Why can a Conv2d layer reproduce a Sobel filter?
options: A convolution layer applies a learned kernel; setting its weights to Sobel gives the same operation
questions.explain: CNNs learn kernels instead of hand-designing them.

questions.q: For input size W, kernel K, padding P and stride S, what's the output size?
What does max pooling provide?
options: Down-sampling and some tolerance to small shifts
questions.explain: It keeps the strongest response in each window.

questions.q: What is a receptive field?
options: The region of the input that influences a unit; it grows with stacked layers

questions.q: Why does weight sharing make convolutions parameter-efficient?
options: The same kernel is reused at every position instead of one weight per pixel connection
questions.explain: Compare a conv layer with an equivalent fully connected one.

questions.q: How do you count a Conv2d layer's parameters?
options: out_channels * (in_channels * kh * kw) + out_channels bias terms

questions.q: Why run a random batch through a new model first?
options: To confirm tensor shapes before training

questions.q: What does flattening do before fully connected layers?
options: Reshapes feature maps into a vector
questions.explain: The linear layer expects a fixed size.

questions.q: Why evaluate on a test set the model never saw?
options: Training accuracy can be inflated by memorization; test accuracy estimates generalization
questions.explain: Held-out data is the honest estimate.

questions.q: Why did the lesson switch from CIFAR-10 to FashionMNIST?
options: The CIFAR-10 mirror was too slow to download in that environment

questions.q: What does the loss function do during training?
options: Measures how wrong predictions are so gradients can update weights

questions.q: Why shuffle training data each epoch?
options: So batches aren't ordered and the model doesn't learn order artefacts

questions.q: What gap signals overfitting?
options: Training accuracy much higher than test accuracy
questions.explain: The gap grows over epochs without regularization.

questions.q: What does dropout do?
options: Randomly zeroes activations during training to reduce co-adaptation

questions.q: What did the lesson learn about heavy regularization on this dataset?
options: It can trade off accuracy by underfitting; regularization isn't free

questions.q: Why seed both models identically?
options: So differences come from regularization, not random initialization

questions.q: What problem do residual (skip) connections address?
options: Training very deep networks by letting gradients flow through identity shortcuts

questions.q: ResNet-50 vs ResNet-18: what differs?
options: ResNet-50 is deeper with many more parameters

questions.q: Both ResNets predicted something wrong for the astronaut photo. What does the lesson conclude?
options: ImageNet has no 'person' class, so they're forced to pick something else: out-of-distribution input

questions.q: What is a pretrained backbone?
options: A network already trained on a large dataset (e.g. ImageNet), reused as a feature extractor

questions.q: What's frozen-backbone transfer learning?
options: Keep pretrained layers fixed and train only the new final layer

questions.q: When does full fine-tuning tend to beat frozen features?
options: When the target domain differs and you have enough data to adapt all layers

questions.q: Why adapt ResNet-18 for FashionMNIST input?
options: The dataset is grayscale (1 channel) while ResNet expects 3
questions.explain: Change the first conv or replicate channels.

questions.q: What is a sensible lr for fine-tuning pretrained layers?
options: Smaller than training from scratch, to avoid destroying useful features

questions.q: Why isn't a single accuracy figure enough?
options: It can hide that some classes are much worse than others

questions.q: What does a confusion matrix show?
options: How often each true class is predicted as each class

questions.q: Precision for a class means...
options: Of everything predicted as that class, the share that was right
Of all true members, the share found
questions.explain: Recall is the share of true members found.

questions.q: Why reload the saved checkpoint to re-evaluate?
options: To independently confirm the number instead of trusting the training script's print

questions.q: What does an input-gradient saliency map show?
options: Which input pixels most affect the prediction

questions.q: What is Grad-CAM-style visualization based on?
options: Last convolutional layer activations weighted by gradients, giving a coarse heat map

questions.q: Why check attention maps against real pixel content?
options: A heat map story can sound plausible but not hold up (e.g. attention on background)

questions.q: What was the lesson's first result?
options: Surprising, so it was investigated rather than accepted

questions.q: A class has 30 training images versus ~6,000 for the others. What's the expected effect?
options: The minority class is poorly learned and under-predicted with a standard loss

questions.q: What does a class-weighted loss do?
What's a risk of heavy class weights?
options: More false positives for the minority class (lower precision)

questions.q: Other fixes for imbalance include...
options: Resampling and targeted augmentation of the minority class

questions.q: How was the capstone configuration chosen?
options: From earlier findings: heavy augmentation and dropout underfit, so use a lighter touch

questions.q: What does independent final evaluation add?
options: An unbiased estimate on held-out test data
questions.explain: Don't tune on the test set.

questions.q: Why track train and test curves every epoch?
options: To see overfitting or underfitting as it develops

questions.q: What's flip-only augmentation's rationale for FashionMNIST?
What is IoU?
options: Intersection over Union: overlap area divided by combined area of two boxes

questions.q: Two 10x10 boxes overlap by half (x from 0-10 and 5-15). What's the IoU?
What are anchors?
options: Predefined boxes of several scales and ratios that a detector refines

questions.q: Why verify IoU against hand-computed cases first?
options: Wrong IoU would quietly corrupt every later metric

questions.q: Faster R-CNN trained on COCO detects how many classes?
options: 91 category ids (80 used) in COCO's label space

questions.q: What does a detection output include?
options: Boxes, class labels and confidence scores

questions.q: How should a detector behave on a blank image?
options: Ideally return no confident detections, unlike a classifier that always picks a class

questions.q: Why threshold detections by score?
options: To drop low-confidence boxes that are likely false positives

questions.q: What does semantic segmentation output?
options: A class label for every pixel

questions.q: Why isn't pixel accuracy enough?
options: Large background classes dominate, hiding bad performance on small objects

questions.q: How is per-class IoU computed?
options: Pixels correct for the class divided by the union of predicted and true pixels of that class

questions.q: Why use tiny hand-verifiable examples?
options: So every number can be checked by eye

questions.q: DeepLabV3 outputs what compared with a detector?
options: A per-pixel class map instead of bounding boxes

questions.q: How do you get the mask from output logits?
questions.explain: Each pixel gets the highest-scoring class.

questions.q: How many classes does the VOC-trained model use?
What does segmentation give that detection doesn't?
options: The object's exact shape, not just a rectangle

questions.q: Two people stand side by side. What does semantic segmentation say?
options: Both are 'person' pixels with no separation between individuals

questions.q: What does Mask R-CNN add?
options: A separate mask per detected instance

questions.q: When do you need instance segmentation?
options: When you must count or track individual objects of the same class

questions.q: What's the cost of instance segmentation?
options: More compute and a more complex model

questions.q: How many keypoints does COCO pose use?
questions.explain: Nose, eyes, ears, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, ankles.

questions.q: The astronaut photo is cropped at chest height. What did confidence scores reveal?
options: Which keypoints were actually visible versus guessed

questions.q: Why filter keypoints by confidence?
options: Low-confidence points can be wildly wrong

questions.q: What can pose estimation feed?
What does optical flow estimate?
options: Apparent motion of pixels between frames
questions.explain: A motion vector per point or pixel.

questions.q: What's the difference between Lucas-Kanade and dense flow?
options: Lucas-Kanade tracks sparse points; dense flow estimates motion for every pixel

questions.q: Why use a known exact pixel shift as a test?
options: It provides ground truth to measure algorithm accuracy

questions.q: What assumption does flow rely on?
options: Brightness constancy and small motion between frames

questions.q: What did OpenCV 5.0 no longer expose?
options: The classic CSRT and KCF trackers
questions.explain: Same kind of removal as Haar cascades.

questions.q: Why was an identical-looking distractor placed close to the target?
options: To test whether tracking survives visual ambiguity

questions.q: What helps trackers survive ambiguity?
options: Motion models and re-detection or association logic

questions.q: Why use a synthetic video with a known trajectory?
options: You can measure tracking error exactly

questions.q: What's the first OCR check in the lesson?
options: Exact match on clean rendered text, to establish a baseline

questions.q: Which degradations did the lesson apply?
options: Blur, rotation and noise, measuring character accuracy

questions.q: Does OCR degrade uniformly?
options: No, different degradations break it at different points

questions.q: How do you improve OCR before recognition?
options: Deskew, denoise and threshold the image

questions.q: What are the pipeline's stages?
options: Detect the sign, track it across frames, then OCR its text

questions.q: Why track instead of detecting every frame?
options: Tracking is cheaper and keeps identity across frames

questions.q: The video is synthetic. Is that disclosed?
options: Yes: stages are real, the input video is synthetic, stated plainly

questions.q: What can go wrong in multi-stage pipelines?
options: Errors compound: a bad detection ruins tracking and OCR
questions.explain: Evaluate each stage and the whole.

questions.q: How does ViT-B/16 turn an image into tokens?
options: It splits it into 16x16 patches and embeds each patch linearly

questions.q: The astronaut photo is out-of-distribution for ImageNet classifiers. Why?
options: ImageNet has no 'person' class, so any prediction is forced into another class

questions.q: What's a trade-off of ViTs versus CNNs?
options: ViTs have fewer inductive biases and usually need more data or pretraining

questions.q: What does self-attention let a ViT do?
options: Relate every patch to every other patch globally
questions.explain: Global context from the first layer.

questions.q: What's an image embedding?
options: A vector from a network's penultimate layer capturing visual features

questions.q: What does cosine similarity compare?
options: The angle between two vectors, ignoring length

questions.q: Why can nearest neighbours look counter-intuitive?
options: Embeddings capture what the network learned, which may not match human notions of similarity
questions.explain: The lesson investigated an unexpected pattern.

questions.q: How would you scale similarity search to millions of images?
options: An approximate nearest-neighbour index (e.g. a vector database)
questions.explain: Exact scan is O(n) per query.

questions.q: How does a prototypical classifier classify with few labels?
options: Average each class's support embeddings into a prototype and assign the nearest

questions.q: Why is it 'remarkably effective' here?
options: Good pretrained embeddings already separate classes; few examples just locate prototypes

questions.q: What's self-supervised learning?
options: Learning representations from unlabeled data using a pretext task

questions.q: When does few-shot fail?
options: When embeddings don't capture the distinction the new classes need

questions.q: In a GAN, what do the two networks do?
options: The generator makes fakes; the discriminator tries to tell fake from real

questions.q: The lesson's discriminator was still winning after 10 epochs. What does that suggest?
options: Training hadn't reached balance, so generation quality was still limited

questions.q: Why evaluate the generator with an independent trained classifier?
options: Judging by eye is subjective; a classifier gives a quantitative signal

questions.q: What's the core idea of diffusion models?
options: Learn to reverse a gradual noising process to generate images

questions.q: Precision@k means...
options: Of the top k results, the share that are relevant
questions.explain: Recall@k is the share of all relevant items found in the top k.

questions.q: Recall@k means...
options: Of all relevant items, the share found in the top k

questions.q: What is mode collapse?
options: A generator producing a few repeated patterns instead of varied outputs

questions.q: How did the lesson measure diversity?
options: Pairwise embedding distances among generated images

questions.q: Why does batching raise throughput?
options: Hardware processes many images in parallel, amortizing overhead
questions.explain: 256 single calls versus one batched call.

questions.q: What's the trade-off of large batches?
options: Higher per-request latency and diminishing returns past a peak

questions.q: Why measure rather than assume throughput?
options: Hardware and model details create real peaks and plateaus

questions.q: Which metric matters for an interactive app?
options: Tail latency (e.g. p95) for single requests

questions.q: What is an FGSM attack?
options: Adding a small perturbation in the direction of the loss gradient's sign to fool the model
questions.explain: Tiny, imperceptible changes can flip predictions.

questions.q: What does adversarial vulnerability imply?
options: Models can fail on inputs humans find nearly identical

questions.q: Which common failure mode is distribution shift?
options: Test data differing from training (lighting, camera, domain)

questions.q: How can you improve robustness?
options: Augmentation, adversarial training and testing under realistic perturbations

questions.q: What's a well-documented bias mechanism the lesson tested?
options: Differential accuracy under varied conditions such as brightness
questions.explain: Performance gaps across groups or conditions.

questions.q: Why report accuracy per subgroup?
options: An overall average can hide large gaps for some groups

questions.q: What's a common source of bias in vision systems?
What should you do when you find a gap?
options: Document it, improve data/model and decide whether the use is appropriate

questions.q: When is a classical CV pipeline the right choice?
options: Controlled setting, simple well-defined task and little data (e.g. a document scanner)
questions.explain: Simple beats complex when it works.

questions.q: When do you reach for a pretrained deep model?
options: Complex variation and enough data or a good pretrained backbone

questions.q: What should you try first on a new problem?
options: The simplest baseline that could work, then measure

questions.q: What factors guide the choice?
options: Data available, accuracy needs, latency, hardware and maintainability

questions.q: What does the capstone combine?
options: A trained classifier within an automated quality-control pipeline

questions.q: Why define metrics before deployment?
options: So pass/fail decisions and costs of errors are explicit
questions.explain: False passes and false rejects cost differently.

questions.q: How should a QC system handle low-confidence items?
What should you monitor after deployment?
options: Input drift and accuracy against periodic labeled samples
